key_insight: A cascaded diffusion model can generate controllable 4D cardiac MRI by separating anatomy from motion, producing anatomically consistent synthetic sequences.
clinical_relevance: This could improve training data for cardiac MRI segmentation and make models more robust across vendors and limited annotation settings.
method: Semi-supervised VAE learns compact anatomical latent space and predicts aligned segmentation masks.
Static latent diffusion generates subject-specific anatomy conditioned on diagnosis and volume measures.
Residual motion diffusion adds temporally coherent cardiac motion across the 4D sequence.
evidence_signal: Across multiple datasets, the approach achieved strong anatomy control (Pearson r > 0.8) and temporal coherence (FVD = 288.08), and synthetic augmentation improved nnU-Net segmentation results.
watch_item: Synthetic data may not fully capture rare pathology or scanner-specific artifacts, so external validation and careful integration into training pipelines are important.
paper_title: Anatomy-Guided Residual Motion Diffusion for Controllable 4D Cardiac MRI Synthesis
